# Model Development Document: Consumer Instalment Loan Decision Model

*Structured after the US Federal Reserve / OCC Supervisory Guidance on Model Risk Management (SR 11-7 / OCC 2011-12). Generated by `make run`; every figure below is read from `results/metrics.json`.*
**All data in this document is SYNTHETIC.** It was generated by a seeded simulator because the public HMDA and German Credit sources were unreachable from the build network; no real applicant is described.

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Model name | `reweighing_a0.5` (recommended) |
| Model tier | Tier 1 (credit decisioning, consumer-facing, fair-lending exposure) |
| Intended use | Approve / decline decision on unsecured instalment-loan applications at a fixed approval rate of 70% |
| Not intended for | Pricing, limit setting, marketing pre-screen, collections, any population outside the development scope |
| Decision rule | approve if predicted probability of bad <= 0.1930 (cutoff set on validation months) |
| Status | **Not ready for deployment**: out-of-time minimum AIR 0.776 is below 0.80 (red monitoring band) |

## 0. Conclusion for the model risk committee

- The GBM candidate is only marginally more accurate than the incumbent scorecard (out-of-time AUC 0.768 vs 0.765) and both show large disparate impact (minimum AIR 0.599 and 0.573).
- Most of the gap is driven by the geography proxy: dropping it (the less-discriminatory alternative) raises minimum AIR to 0.762 at an AUC cost of 0.005.
- The recommended model `reweighing_a0.5` (chosen on validation data by a pre-set rule) reaches minimum AIR 0.776 [0.747, 0.807] out of time, with AUC 0.763.
- It does **not** pass the four-fifths screen out of time (it did on validation: 0.804). The strongest single-model alternative that does pass on the test months is `reweighing_a2` (AIR 0.806, AUC 0.758); it was not chosen because selection must not use test data. Group-specific thresholds would close the gap but are disparate treatment. Recommendation: do not deploy; re-run the LDA search with stronger in-training constraints and a validation margin above 0.80, and investigate the label bias in the recorded outcomes.

## 1. Purpose and scope

The lender is replacing a weight-of-evidence (WOE) logistic scorecard with a gradient-boosted model. Regulation B (ECOA) and the Fair Housing Act prohibit disparate treatment and require review of disparate impact; Regulation B section 1002.9 requires specific principal reasons for adverse action. This document records the data, methodology, testing, limitations and monitoring of the recommended model so that model validation, compliance and the model risk committee can challenge it.

## 2. Data

- **Source / path used:** `synthetic_generator`. Attempts: hmda: failed (URLError: <urlopen error Tunnel connection failed: 403 Forbidden>); german_credit: failed (URLError: <urlopen error Tunnel connection failed: 403 Forbidden>); synthetic_generator: ok.
- **Volume and split:** 40,000 applications. time: train months 1-14, validation 15-18, out-of-time test 19-24 (23,547 / 6,586 / 9,867). The test months are out-of-time and include simulated macro drift.
- **Target:** `bad` = 1 if the loan was recorded as defaulted. Recorded bad rate 15.7%; by group: A 10.6%, B 26.6%, C 20.6%.
- **Protected attributes:** `group` (reference `A`; shares A 62.2%, B 22.9%, C 15.0%), plus sex and age band. They are **never model inputs**; they are held out for the fairness audit only, as a lender would hold self-reported or BISG-imputed demographics.
- **Known data issues:**
  - *Historical label bias.* The simulator records a bad outcome for some applicants who would have repaid, more often in groups B and C and in historically redlined areas. The unbiased bad rate is 11.4% (by group: A 10.2%, B 13.8%, C 12.6%), so 27.6% of recorded bads are spurious. In real data this is unobservable; it is kept here so that the effect of training on biased labels can be measured.
  - *Proxy variables.* `zip_cluster` (geography) is strongly associated with group membership through residential segregation (section 6.3).
  - *Reject inference.* Outcomes exist only for booked loans in real portfolios; this build does not perform reject inference.

## 3. Methodology

1. **Baseline (incumbent): WOE scorecard.** Quantile binning (up to 6 bins), smoothed WOE, L2 logistic regression, scaled to 600 points at 50:1 odds with 20 points to double the odds. Reason codes by points-below-maximum.
2. **Challenger: LightGBM** (300 trees, learning rate 0.05, 15 leaves, row/column subsampling 0.8), unconstrained and with **monotone constraints** in the business-expected direction for every numeric feature (utilisation, DTI, delinquencies, inquiries, loan amount increase risk; history, income, employment, savings, time at address decrease it).
3. **Fair-lending testing:** adverse impact ratio (AIR, four-fifths rule), demographic-parity difference and equalised-odds difference (Fairlearn), with 95% nonparametric bootstrap CIs (1000 resamples).
4. **Less-discriminatory-alternative (LDA) search:** monotone GBMs over feature sets (with / without geography and the strongest remaining proxies) and two complexities; select on validation the highest AIR within 0.02 AUC of the candidate.
5. **Mitigation on the LDA-selected feature set:** reweighing (Kamiran and Calders; strengths [0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0]), exponentiated gradient with a demographic-parity bound (Agarwal et al.; bounds [0.1, 0.05, 0.03, 0.02, 0.01]), and threshold optimisation (Hardt et al.; demographic parity and equalised odds).
6. **Selection rule (validation data only):** highest validation AUC among single, explainable, monotone GBMs within the AUC tolerance whose validation AIR >= 0.80. Threshold optimisation is excluded because it applies group-specific cutoffs (disparate treatment under ECOA); exponentiated gradient is excluded because its randomised mixture of up to 30 classifiers cannot produce stable, specific adverse-action reasons.
7. **Explanations:** exact TreeSHAP (log-odds of bad) per declined applicant; the four largest contributions toward decline become ranked reason codes. Counterfactuals: exhaustive grid search (12 steps per feature) over single and paired changes to actionable features only (credit_utilization, debt_to_income, num_inquiries_6m, loan_amount, savings_balance), cost in IQR units.

## 4. Performance testing (out-of-time test months)

| Model | AUC | Gini | KS | Brier | Bad rate among approved | Min AIR [95% CI] |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| WOE scorecard (incumbent) | 0.765 | 0.531 | 0.407 | 0.1249 | 9.5% | 0.573 [0.546, 0.601] |
| GBM monotone (candidate) | 0.768 | 0.536 | 0.402 | 0.1244 | 9.2% | 0.599 [0.572, 0.626] |
| **`reweighing_a0.5` (recommended)** | 0.763 | 0.527 | 0.396 | 0.1252 | 9.2% | 0.776 [0.747, 0.807] |

Against the (normally unobservable) unbiased outcome the recommended model's AUC is 0.749 vs 0.737 for the candidate: part of the candidate's apparent accuracy on recorded labels is accuracy at reproducing historical bias.

**Monotonicity:** share of sampled applicants whose predicted risk moves only in the expected direction along each feature: unconstrained GBM worst feature 0.0%, monotone GBM worst feature 100.0%.

## 5. Stability

- Score PSI, training vs out-of-time test: recommended 0.061 (**stable**); scorecard 0.050.
- Largest feature shifts: num_inquiries_6m 0.172, credit_utilization 0.051, debt_to_income 0.022 (bands: < 0.10 stable, 0.10-0.25 monitor, > 0.25 action).

### 6.3 Proxy discrimination analysis

- Geography alone predicts protected-group membership with AUC 0.835; all candidate features together 0.870, and 0.681 without geography. The remaining signal comes from income, credit history and other legitimately risk-related features, which carry structural group gaps.
- Geography accounts for 10.2% of the candidate's mean absolute SHAP. Removing it (LDA search) moved the minimum AIR from 0.599 to 0.762 on the test months.
- The recommended model contains no geographic feature.

### 6.4 Secondary attributes

sex (reference M): AIR F 0.972; age_band (reference <62): AIR 62+ 1.353.

## 7. Explainability and adverse action

- Every declined test applicant (3,314) receives exactly four ranked reason codes (3,314 with four codes); for 99.5% all four push towards decline. SHAP additivity error 0.0e+00.
- Reason codes agree with the incumbent scorecard's points-below-max method on the principal reason for 72.8% of applicants declined by both (top-4 overlap 74.5%).
- Counterfactual ("what would change the decision") found for 99.9% of declined applicants within the actionable bounds; 44.9% need a single change. See `adverse_action_examples.md`.

## 8. Limitations and assumptions

- Data is synthetic. Effect sizes (label bias, segregation strength, drift) are design choices of the simulator, not estimates about any real market.
- The four-fifths rule is an EEOC employment screen used here as a conventional disparate-impact flag; it is not a legal safe harbour in US lending, where the test is whether a less-discriminatory alternative exists.
- AIR is computed at one approval rate (70%); disparity changes with the cutoff and must be re-tested if the cutoff moves.
- Group membership is assumed known for testing; real lenders must use self-reported (HMDA) or proxy (BISG) demographics, which add measurement error to every fairness number.
- Reweighing uses the protected attribute in training only. Legal review must confirm this is acceptable in the target jurisdiction.
- Counterfactuals are on a grid and assume features can move independently; they are not advice and ignore feasibility costs.
- No reject inference; through-the-door population differs from booked population.
- Approval-rate parity is not the same as equal error rates; equalised-odds difference for the recommended model is 0.097.

## 9. Ongoing monitoring plan

| Metric | Frequency | Green | Amber (investigate) | Red (escalate to model risk committee) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Score PSI vs development | monthly | < 0.10 | 0.10-0.25 | > 0.25 |
| Feature PSI (each input) | monthly | < 0.10 | 0.10-0.25 | > 0.25 |
| Minimum AIR (each protected group) | monthly / quarterly with CI | >= 0.90 | 0.80-0.90 | < 0.80 or CI upper bound < 0.80 |
| AUC on matured vintages | quarterly | within 0.02 of development | 0.02-0.05 drop | > 0.05 drop |
| Reason-code distribution | monthly | stable | rank-1 share shift > 10 pp | new prohibited-basis reason appears |
| Override rate | monthly | < 5% | 5-10% | > 10% |

Evidence from the out-of-time months: score PSI 0.061; monthly minimum AIR of the recommended model ranged down to 0.737 (see `figures/monitoring_psi_air.png`).

## 10. Validation evidence

- Unit and integration tests (`make test`): WOE/IV correctness, PSI properties, Fairlearn cross-check of the vectorised bootstrap metrics, reweighing balance, SHAP additivity, four reason codes for every decline, counterfactual validity (each returned counterfactual is approved by the model and only touches actionable features), monotonicity, HMDA/German parsers, and an end-to-end smoke run.
- Out-of-time evaluation on months never used for training, cutoff setting or model selection.
- Selection decisions (LDA, recommended model) used validation data only.
